name: Phoenicia
description: A star 20 parsecs away, 75% of the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 99711: radius 0.752 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 0.306 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.051) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 99711: effective temperature 4955 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.031)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 4.61 from 2025A&A...698A..93J; the 28 published values span log g 4.14 to 4.76, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 99711: distance 19.677 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.005), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 20 parsecs away, 75% of the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 0.306 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,955 K, so 0.752 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 99711: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: HD 192263
quotes.card: HD 192263, also named Phoenicia, is a star with an orbiting exoplanet in the equatorial constellation of Aquila.
quotes.introduction: The system is located at a distance of 64 light-years from the Sun based on parallax measurements, and is drifting further away with a radial velocity of −10.7 km/s.
